# Feedback-Control Comparison Admission (Provisional)

## Scope and Authority

This chapter records the F01 (#11785) **admission contract**, not a qualified
matching calculation. `src/config/engine_model_inventory.json` is the package
authority; `src/engines/feedback_comparison.py` derives required model/variant/
drive rows from it. Every registered package remains in the program denominator.
Required capability, declared support, runtime availability, and scientific
qualification are separate fields. An unavailable engine stays required and
unqualified. The calculation registry remains blocked for release.

The common forward-dynamics form is

$$
M(q;\theta)\dot v + h(q,v;\theta)
= S(q)^T\tau + J_c(q)^T\lambda + f_{\mathrm{external}},
\qquad \dot q=N(q)v.
$$

Here $q$ may lie on a configuration manifold and need not have the dimension
of $v$. A muscle plant replaces direct generalized effort with an excitation
input $e(t)$, internal activation/tendon/fiber state $z$, and a state-dependent
mapping $\tau=\tau(q,v,z,e;\theta_m)$. Recorded torque cannot be substituted
for excitation, or vice versa, as the same native input. Units are SI for
effort and seconds for time; excitation is dimensionless. Force, contact,
instrumented grip, and EMG observations are distinct evidence sources.

## Replay and Comparison Preconditions

An independent replay uses one saved full initial physical state and a
time-only input player with no state feedback or resets. Its model, provider,
physical state schema, execution policy, actuator schema, contact and
integration identities, applied input, observation set, horizon, and channel
order and simulation-relative timebase are bound by SHA-256 evidence. Each
replay receipt also binds the **actual initial-state payload** with the Tools
T01 `integrity.initial_state_sha256` digest under
`feedback-comparison/1.1.0`. Matching state-schema digests alone do not show
that two simulations started from the same physical state. Earlier/unversioned
comparison receipts remain usable for identity and transcription inventory,
but fail closed for independent replay claims. Same-input admission requires
equal initial-state payload digests in addition to equal schemas.
Each
input-channel schema digest includes target, coordinate, unit, and force frame.
Direct torque/force/effort is held
exactly over each integration step; excitation interpolation is declared.
Holding a command does not imply that a state-dependent actuator delivers
constant force. A matching state trajectory from a
transcription is insufficient; the native plant must reproduce it when
integrated separately. The existing `same-input-bundle/v1` has Euclidean
`nq=nv` arrays and does not bind policy and applied-input hashes, so it cannot
qualify this contract. F01 does not alter that older schema.

Identity, transcription-native feasibility, within-engine independent input
reproduction, cross-engine same-input, observation accuracy, and bounded
biomechanical equivalence are separate admission levels. A transcription
receipt does not satisfy an independent replay or observation-score receipt.
Within-engine and same-input replay receipts must cover the declared full
horizon, even when all reported states are present. Observation scoring binds
its own output-sampling grid digest separately from the executed input grid;
capture clocks cannot be inferred from actuator sampling.
Same-input
requires equal physical-model, physics, contact, integrator, actuator,
state-schema, policy, time-grid, input, observation, horizon, and channel identities.
Common rigid-body emulation, native own-contact, and externally forced runs
must keep different evidence-mode labels. The shared full-body OpenSim parity
path removes native ForceSet/ConstraintSet/ContactGeometrySet, and MyoSuite's
shared-body path uses the MuJoCo rigid-body core. Neither establishes native
muscle/contact parity. A restarted 50 ms L2 result cannot establish continuous
full-swing native-muscle replay. Native muscle claims additionally require
muscle-state, contact, and force evidence across an uninterrupted horizon.

The prospective baseline names are independent polynomial, computed torque,
MOSAIC with time-varying LQR, and selected OCP. They must share observation
identity, physical horizon, and compute budget before accuracy or speed can be
compared. No F01 test measures tracking error, pass rate, energy, GRF, grip
load, muscle physiology, or runtime. `tests/unit/engines/test_feedback_comparison.py`
checks admission failures; F09 and later native lanes own numerical receipts.

## F09a Positions-Only Sampling on the Observation Clock

The provisional observation boundary in
`src/shared/python/motion_matching/replay_metrics.py` samples native output
positions at measured-observation times before the existing replay metrics are
evaluated. The native output clock $t_i^n$ and observation clock $t_k^o$ are
separate evidence. For ordered native 3-D marker positions $p_{ij}^n$, the
declared method `linear_position/v1` defines

$$
\hat p_{kj} = (1-\alpha_k)p_{ij}^n + \alpha_k p_{i+1,j}^n,
\qquad
\alpha_k = \frac{t_k^o - t_i^n}{t_{i+1}^n - t_i^n},
\qquad t_i^n \le t_k^o \le t_{i+1}^n.
$$

Both clocks must be finite, strictly increasing, and contain at least two
samples. The observation interval must be contained by the native-output
interval; the sampler rejects extrapolation. Native and measured positions
must declare the same frame, timebase, and ordered marker identities. The
interpolation applies only to 3-D marker positions. It is not a generalized
coordinate, velocity, quaternion, or engine-state integrator. Missing measured
positions retain the existing validity mask; only valid measured entries must
be finite. The exact observation clock is passed to
`compute_replay_five_metrics`, keeping early-window and terminal metrics tied
to the measured clock.

The helper records source, native-output, observation, and alignment hashes so
downstream receipts can identify the arrays and both clocks. These hashes are
content identities, not evidence that a producer is authentic or that the
motion is physically correct. This F09a implementation adds no tolerance,
acceptance threshold, capture approval, engine qualification, or physiology
claim. The calculation inventory remains empty and manual release remains
blocked pending its owner program; this provisional calculation note does not
register or approve a released engineering calculation.

## Uncertainty and Release Boundary

The inventory declares a flexible-club requirement but currently records its
support as unknown. OpenSim's eight-muscle variant factory and MyoSuite's
upstream myo_sim anatomy are declared, not calibrated full-swing physiology.
Provider/model hashes identify code and files, not physical validity. Model
parameters, observation clocks, camera/marker registration, contact forces,
muscle redundancy, and EMG coverage remain unqualified until independent
measured evidence and native replay receipts establish a bounded scope.

## F09b Native Observation Scoring and Full-State Identity

The F09b observation workflow in
`src/engines/feedback_observation_qualification.py` consumes the validated
Tools `ExperimentReplayBundle` schema `experiment-replay/1.0.0` together with
the F01 `ComparisonEvidence`, native marker positions, and measured positions.
Before scoring, the workflow checks that model, provider, full state schema,
ordered channels, input kind/interpolation, timebase, full applied-input
history, input grid, execution policy, replay mode, horizon, and contact
policy agree between the two authorities. The bundle validator independently
checks the complete ordered initial state and all T01 integrity hashes.
Generalized position and velocity dimensions are checked separately against
F01's `nq` and `nv`; no Euclidean `nq=nv` assumption is made.

F01c's versioned `feedback-comparison/1.1.0` replay contract carries T01's
actual `initial_state_sha256` separately from the state-schema digest. F09b
requires that payload hash to equal the actual bundle hash before admission;
the F09 source identity also binds model-identity and capability-declaration
digests. Replacing the initial state while keeping its schema fixed changes
the source identity; changing an input or policy without changing the F01
evidence is rejected. No identity is constructed from only the state schema
or from selected coordinates.

The workflow samples only native 3-D marker positions onto the retained
observation clock through the F09a positions-only interpolation helper, then
uses the existing `compute_replay_five_metrics`, pelvis-yaw metric, and
`motion_matching.acceptance.evaluate` gate contract. The receipt binds T01's
initial-state digest, F01 evidence identity, native and observed positions,
both clocks, retained observation times, alignment, metric results, frozen
criterion identifiers, and acceptance verdict. It does not add thresholds or
interpret a transport-valid bundle as a physics result. The content-addressed
native acceptance receipt and explicit capture are bound into the score and
criterion identities. F01c observation-accuracy admission receives the exact
F09a retained observation-time-grid digest after scoring; raw paths or private
receipt fields are not copied to the public summary.

The report retains each registered required model/variant/drive row and the
six-engine denominator. Missing native output, unavailable capability, or an
unqualified F01 row remains visible and cannot become a pass or zero score.
Observation scoring does not set the registry qualification field. A passing
numerical gate is only reported as accepted by the existing gate evaluator;
campaign qualification remains false until every required registry row is
qualified and every existing gate passes. Synthetic contract fixtures prove
identity binding and sampling behavior but provide no physiological or
cross-engine acceptance evidence.

## F09c Strict Native Replay Execution

The F09c execution boundary in
`src/engines/feedback_native_execution.py` consumes one frozen Tools T01
`ExperimentReplayBundle` and one explicit adapter binding for an existing F01
inventory row. The binding preserves two identities: F01's inventoried
package, variant, source and provider; and T01's native model, adapter provider,
loaded-model digest, state schema, channel schema, and ordered actuator IDs.
The two provider identities are not interchangeable. Bindings are explicit;
the executor never infers a full-body mapping from the adapter's synthetic
unit-hinge test identifiers.

Current execution support is limited to the reviewed MuJoCo and Drake
direct-torque adapter pairs. The report retains every inventory row and all
six required engines, marking rows without an adapter or with unavailable
runtime evidence as blocking. Before stepping, the bundle must declare
native-own-contact replay, no observation or state-feedback access, reset
policy forbidden, simulation-relative time, and zero-order-held actuator
torque. The executor calls only the adapter selected by the binding and checks
the actual full output against exact initial-state, input, policy, channel,
model, and time-grid identities. It also checks the complete native numerical
initialization state, full horizon, finite values, and generalized effort
dimensions without assuming `nq == nv`.

The versioned execution receipt records content digests and execution facts,
not a scientific verdict. Local model paths are excluded. The declared
`state_reset_allowed=False` policy is kept separate from the unknown reset
counter (`state_reset_count=None`); a forbidden-reset policy is not a measured
zero. A successful receipt remains `unqualified`; it cannot establish marker accuracy,
physiological validity, muscle/contact capability, or cross-engine
equivalence. Contract tests execute a synthetic one-hinge model using the
actual adapter, but do not qualify any registered production model. The
calculation registry remains blocked; this execution interface is not a
released matching calculation.

F09d (#11907) adds the next boundary: explicit model-owned forward kinematics
from those native output configurations to named 3-D marker positions. Its
ordered local-point map and source/loaded-model/provider identities are
content-addressed; generalized coordinates are never treated as marker
positions. See
`manuals/upstreamdrift/chapters/28-native-marker-forward-kinematics.qmd`.
